title: How CRE Leasing Pros Can Take AI to the Next Level
excerpt: AI is moving beyond routine automation in CRE, letting leasing pros work at scale while keeping human judgement in the loop.
content_html:
This story was originally published on CRE Daily. Join 70,000+ commercial real estate professionals getting daily news, market insights, and industry analysis delivered straight to their inbox with the free CRE Daily newsletter.

Key Takeaways

  • AI tools in commercial real estate are moving past routine task automation and into continuous, portfolio-wide monitoring of leases, contracts, and compliance documents.

  • Centralizing data that once lived in one person's inbox or filing system lets entire teams surface answers, spot risks, and act on information faster.

  • The strongest AI workflows keep humans in the loop for final decisions, with AI handling extraction and monitoring while professionals apply judgement.

Historically, commercial property businesses have had to contend with the paperwork and data that sit at the heart of property management. Teams manage large volumes of leases, tenant correspondence, invoices, maintenance records, compliance documents, insurance certificates and other property records, often spread across different systems and formats.

Much of that information needs to be entered, checked, and kept up to date manually. With so much data to manage, property teams have historically had to prioritize what gets reviewed and accept that some information will inevitably go unchecked.

AI is beginning to change that equation. The opportunity isn't simply to make existing processes faster. It is to make it practical to extract, compare and monitor information across an entire portfolio, including work that would previously have been too time-consuming or expensive to do at scale.

Is automating routine tasks as good as it gets?

Many CRE firms use AI tools to speed up routine, everyday tasks that often end up taking large chunks of time. By outsourcing these processes to AI, professionals are freed up to spend time on other, higher-level tasks, thereby speeding up workflows and increasing workflows, productivity, and sales volume.

Companies are increasingly recognizing how AI can be used to automate repetitive manual processes and support CRE professionals. According to JLL's recent Global Future of Work survey, 78 percent of business and CRE leaders see AI as something that will significantly impact their portfolio strategies and how their business functions over the next 3 to 5 years.

However, only 15 percent reported having moved beyond exploring AI tools and initial deployment to actively integrating AI into CRE operations. As companies around the world continue to assess how AI can be implemented into their operations, innovative AI offerings are emerging that can do much more than just automate routine tasks. So what does it look like when AI moves beyond automating the tasks everyone already knows about?
